problem: The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\frac{1}{1-\pi x}$ about $x=0$ is
worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(0)+{f}^{′}(0)(x-0)+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(0)(x-0)^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ and ${f}^{″}(0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{1-\pi x}=(1-\pi x)^{-1} & ⟹ &  & f(0) & =1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\pi (1-\pi x)^{-2} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =\pi  \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =2{\pi }^{2}(1-\pi x)^{-3} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =2{\pi }^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(0),$ ${f}^{′}(0),$ and ${f}^{″}(0)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =1+\pi \cdot x+2{\pi }^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2} \\  & =1+\pi x+{\pi }^{2}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
